content_sections.heading: About AUD
content_sections.text: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar University Delhi is a State University set up through an Act of the Legislature of the National Capital Territory of Delhi. Its Kashmere Gate Campus is on Lothian Road, Delhi. The posts are at the Centre for Psychotherapy and Clinical Research (CPCR) under the School of Human Studies.

content_sections.heading: AUD Psychotherapist Eligibility 2026
content_sections.text: M.A. in Psychology with at least 55% marks or an equivalent GPA from a recognized university. M.Phil in Clinical Psychology / M.Phil in Psychoanalytic Psychotherapy / M.Phil in Psychotherapy and Clinical Thinking, or post-master's training, degree or diploma with specialization in psychotherapy, clinical practice or counselling. At least two years of experience in clinical practice / psychotherapeutic work and/or counselling in the field of mental health, at public or private institutions, universities, hospitals, clinics or NGOs. Internships done as part of an academic programme do not count as valid work experience. You must hold the essential qualifications as on the closing date of application. Ph.D. in Clinical Psychology / PsyD (Doctor of Psychology) / Ph.D. with demonstrable interest in psychodynamic and psychoanalytical work. Experience in teaching and supervising trainee counsellors, psychotherapists or clinical psychologists. Evidence of research or publications in psychotherapy or clinical practice. Well-developed sensitivity, empathy, regard and in-depth understanding of the human psyche. For the full eligibility conditions of the post, see the official notification.

content_sections.heading: Job Description
content_sections.text: Psychometric screening of first-year batches of all programmes to identify psychologically vulnerable students, through a Mentor-Mentee System, a Buddy System and other preventive mechanisms. Psychotherapy and clinical counselling for students. Clinical supervision, administrative and organisational work, and community mental health work. Intellectual and practice-based processes and activities. Adopting and implementing a uniform mental health policy, drawing on the UMMEED Draft Guidelines, the MANODARPAN initiative and the National Suicide Prevention Strategy. Consistent, informal and confidential support to students, especially during examinations and academic transitions. Protocols for immediate referral to mental health services, local hospitals and suicide prevention helplines. Training teaching and non-teaching staff in psychological first aid, spotting warning signs, responding to self-harm and making referrals. Training teaching, non-teaching and administrative staff to work with students from vulnerable and marginalised backgrounds in a sensitive, inclusive and non-discriminatory way. Confidential, accessible mechanisms for reporting, redressing and preventing sexual assault, harassment, ragging and bullying on the basis of caste, class, gender, sexual orientation, disability, religion or ethnicity, and psycho-social support to victims. Sensitisation programmes (physical and/or online) for parents and guardians on student mental health. Adding mental health literacy, emotional regulation, life skills and awareness of support services to orientation programmes and co-curricular activities. Keeping anonymised records and preparing an annual report on wellness interventions, referrals, training sessions and mental health activities. Regular career counselling for students and parents that is inclusive and sensitive to socio-economic and psychological contexts, plus structured academic planning and mechanisms for monitoring and accountability. Any other duties assigned by the Competent Authority.

content_sections.heading: Selection Process
content_sections.text: Meeting the minimum qualifications does not guarantee an interview call. If many applications come in, the university may shortlist candidates based on qualifications or experience above the minimum, or on other criteria it decides. Only shortlisted candidates are invited for interview. All appointments are provisional until certificates are verified. Documents and antecedents may be checked at the interview, at joining or at any time during service.

content_sections.heading: Service Conditions
content_sections.text: The engagement is purely on a visiting basis. It depends on the requirement of CPCR and on terms approved by the university. Applicants working in Government or Public Sector Undertakings (including Boards and Autonomous Bodies) must submit a No Objection Certificate on the prescribed proforma at the interview, if they did not upload it with the online application. If any information turns out to be false or concealed, the services will be terminated immediately. The university may also take action under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. Canvassing in any form leads to disqualification. Applications that are incomplete or do not meet the qualifications will be rejected summarily. The university may revise, reschedule, cancel, suspend or withdraw the recruitment in part or in full. Disputes fall under the territorial jurisdiction of the High Court of Delhi.

content_sections.heading: How to Apply for AUD Psychotherapist Recruitment 2026
content_sections.text: Documents to include: Mark-sheets of all educational qualifications claimed in the online form. Clear evidence of your professional qualification, showing the nature and duration of the post-master's degree, diploma or training. Experience certificates of clinical practice showing the period (from–to) and the nature of the work. No Objection Certificate, if you are employed in Government or a PSU. Hard copies that arrive late are rejected, and the university is not responsible for postal delays. Questions about the online application go to [email protected] .

faq.question: Q1. How much does an AUD Psychotherapist earn?
faq.answer: Rs.4,200/- for each full-day visit, with a ceiling of Rs.85,000/- per month, as per University norms.

faq.question: Q2. Is this a regular job?
faq.answer: No. The engagement is purely on a visiting basis and depends on the requirement of the Centre for Psychotherapy and Clinical Research.

faq.question: Q3. What minimum marks do I need in my M.A.?
faq.answer: At least 55% marks or an equivalent GPA in M.A. Psychology from a recognized university.

faq.question: Q4. Do internships count towards the two years of experience?
faq.answer: No. Internships done during an academic programme are excluded from valid work experience.

faq.question: Q5. Is an M.Phil compulsory?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. Instead of an M.Phil in Clinical Psychology, Psychoanalytic Psychotherapy, or Psychotherapy and Clinical Thinking, you can have post-master's training, a degree or a diploma specialising in psychotherapy, clinical practice or counselling.

faq.question: Q6. Do I need to send a hard copy after applying online?
faq.answer: Yes. Send the printout with self-attested, indexed and paginated documents to Room No. 31A, Kashmere Gate Campus, Delhi – 110 006, so that it arrives by 17:30 hrs on the last date. That date is four weeks from publication in Employment News.

faq.question: Q7. What should I write on the envelope?
faq.answer: The name of the position (Psychotherapist) and the advertisement number AUD/55-1(151)/Rect./2026/1029, on the top of the envelope.

faq.question: Q8. How will I know my interview date?
faq.answer: Interview dates will be posted on https://aud.delhi.gov.in/ and emailed to shortlisted candidates at the address given in the application form.

faq.question: Q9. What will the Psychotherapist's main work be?
faq.answer: The main work includes psychometric screening of first-year batches, psychotherapy and clinical counselling for students, training staff in psychological first aid, and preparing an annual report on wellness interventions and referrals.

faq.question: Q10. Whom do I contact about problems with the online application?
faq.answer: Email [email protected]. The university does not answer interim correspondence or personal enquiries.
